non_claim: This crosswalk is implementation evidence and repository-readiness guidance. It is not certification, legal advice, formal compliance attestation, or a claim that RuleOak alone satisfies every control in any external framework.

frameworks.name: Model Context Protocol 2026-07-28
frameworks.limitations: RuleOak is an execution/interception boundary, not a complete general-purpose MCP client/server SDK. Compatibility is limited to the protocol surfaces RuleOak actually intercepts/inspects.

mappings.ASI01 Agent Goal Hijack: indirect: deterministic policy boundary limits executable consequences but does not solve prompt/goal hijack
mappings.ASI02 Tool Misuse & Exploitation: direct: exact policy, approvals, one-use authority, capability inspection and effect evidence
mappings.ASI03 Identity & Privilege Abuse: direct/partial: bounded authority, grants/envelopes/revocation; identity systems outside RuleOak remain external
mappings.ASI04 Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerabiliti: partial: capability drift, MCP inspection, dependency/release controls; not a universal software supply-chain scanner
mappings.ASI05 Unexpected Code Execution: partial: deny/approval boundaries and bounded adapters; not an OS sandbox
mappings.ASI06 Memory & Context Poisoning: out_of_scope_directly: evidence/policy can constrain consequences but RuleOak is not a memory-security product
mappings.ASI07 Insecure Inter-Agent Communication: out_of_scope_directly: RuleOak does not provide a complete inter-agent secure messaging protocol
mappings.ASI08 Cascading Failures: direct/partial: CrashLab, bounded authority, evidence-safe retry and duplicate-effect prevention reduce propagation risk
mappings.ASI09 Human-Agent Trust Exploitation: partial: explicit approvals/evidence improve operator visibility but do not solve social/psychological trust exploitation
mappings.ASI10 Rogue Agents: direct/partial: hard execution boundaries, deny override, revocation and one-use authority constrain actions that cross RuleOak

frameworks.name: OWASP Agent Control Standard (public preview, 2026-09-01)
frameworks.limitations: ACS is newly published and evolving. RuleOak does not claim ACS conformance until a stable conformance target and explicit adapter/test suite are implemented.

frameworks.name: OpenSSF OSPS Baseline 2026.08.28
frameworks.limitations: The exact 24 Level-1 controls are tracked individually. Source-pass, hybrid, not-applicable and external-required states are distinct; hosted controls must be verified on the authoritative repository.

frameworks.name: SLSA 1.2
frameworks.limitations: A SLSA level is a property of an actual source/build process and attested artifact. Source configuration alone cannot prove the level before the fresh GitHub repository executes the release workflow.

frameworks.name: NIST Secure Software Development Framework
frameworks.limitations: NIST SSDF is organization/process guidance. RuleOak does not claim NIST certification.
